enum_mappings.description: Shared status enum used across all models. 'Active' contractors are those currently available for work. Deleted (3) are soft-deleted and should be excluded by default.
Same shared status enum. Active customers are registered and usable accounts.
Job lifecycle statuses. A job is considered 'completed/done' when status is IN (11=Completed, 28=Closed, 29=Dropped). Deleted (3) jobs are soft-deleted.
How the job is delivered. One Time = single occurrence, Recurring = repeats on schedule, Scheduled = quoted job with set date.
Service/pricing type. Column is abbreviated as 'serv_type' (not 'service_type'). Note: enum value is spelled 'Houlry' in code but means 'Hourly'.

column_descriptions.description: Foreign key to the customers table (customer who created the job). This is the customer FK — NOT a column called customer_id.
Service/pricing type for the job (Quoted=1, Bid=2, Hourly=3). Abbreviated column name.
The name/label of the job type (e.g., 'Snow Shovelling', 'Lawn Mowing'). Use this column — not 'name'.

business_rules.title: Soft Delete Rule
business_rules.rule: All models use soft deletes via status=3 (Deleted). When counting or listing records, ALWAYS exclude status=3 unless the user explicitly asks for deleted records. This applies to: contractors, customers, jobs, properties, and all other tables with a status column.

business_rules.title: Job Completion Statuses
business_rules.rule: A job is considered 'completed' or 'done' when its status is one of: 11 (Completed), 28 (Closed), or 29 (Dropped). When asked about completed jobs, use: status IN (11, 28, 29).

business_rules.title: Active Contractors Definition
business_rules.rule: An 'active' contractor is one with status=1 (Active) AND status != 3 (not deleted). Simply filtering status=1 is sufficient since status=1 and status=3 are mutually exclusive.

business_rules.title: Active Customers Definition
business_rules.rule: An 'active' customer is one with status=1 (Active). Exclude deleted (status=3) by default.

business_rules.title: Stale Cache Columns — Do Not Use
business_rules.rule: The columns 'completed_jobs', 'completed_jobs_count', 'total_earned', and similar denormalized cache columns on contractors and customers are STALE and contain NULL or 0 values. NEVER use these columns directly. Instead, always JOIN the jobs table and COUNT/SUM to get accurate numbers. For example, to count completed jobs per contractor: JOIN jobs ON contractors.id = jobs.contractor_id WHERE jobs.status IN (11, 28, 29) GROUP BY contractor.

business_rules.title: Service = Job Type (Terminology)
business_rules.rule: When the admin says 'service', 'services', 'most popular service', 'types of services', they mean JOB TYPES from the job_types table (e.g., Snow Shovelling, Lawn Mowing). They do NOT mean service_areas. Query job_types.title to answer questions about services. To find the most popular service, JOIN jobs to job_types and COUNT by job type.

business_rules.title: Jobs to Service Areas — Join Through Properties
business_rules.rule: Jobs connect to service areas THROUGH the properties table: jobs.property_id → properties.id, then properties.service_area_id → service_areas.id. To find which area has the most jobs, JOIN: jobs → properties → service_areas, then GROUP BY service_areas.title. The join_service_areas table is for pricing (maps job_types to service_areas) and does NOT have a job_id column — never use it to link individual jobs to areas.

verified_queries.question: How many active contractors are there?
verified_queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contractors WHERE status = 1
verified_queries.explanation: Active = status 1. Excludes deleted (3), inactive (2), suspended (13), etc.

verified_queries.question: How many total customers are there?
verified_queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE status != 3

verified_queries.question: How many completed snow shovelling jobs are there?
verified_queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM jobs j JOIN job_types jt ON j.job_type_id = jt.id WHERE j.status IN (11, 28, 29) AND jt.title ILIKE '%snow shovel%'
verified_queries.explanation: Completed = status IN (11, 28, 29). Job type matched via job_types.title.

verified_queries.question: How many jobs are currently in progress?
verified_queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM jobs WHERE status IN (8, 9, 10, 18) AND status != 3
verified_queries.explanation: In progress = Accepted (8), Started (9), Paused (10), Resumed (18).

verified_queries.question: How many recurring jobs are there?
verified_queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM jobs WHERE delivery_type = 2 AND status != 3

verified_queries.question: Which contractor has the most completed jobs?
verified_queries.sql: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name, COUNT(j.id) AS completed_jobs FROM contractors c JOIN jobs j ON c.id = j.contractor_id WHERE j.status IN (11, 28, 29) AND c.status = 1 GROUP BY c.id, c.first_name, c.last_name ORDER BY completed_jobs DESC LIMIT 10
verified_queries.explanation: Must JOIN jobs table and COUNT — do NOT use the stale completed_jobs column on contractors.

verified_queries.question: Show me the last 5 cancelled jobs
verified_queries.sql: SELECT j.id, jt.title AS job_type, CONCAT(cu.first_name, ' ', cu.last_name) AS customer, CONCAT(co.first_name, ' ', co.last_name) AS contractor, j.created_at, j.bid_amount FROM jobs j LEFT JOIN job_types jt ON j.job_type_id = jt.id LEFT JOIN customers cu ON j.created_by = cu.id LEFT JOIN contractors co ON j.contractor_id = co.id WHERE j.status = 12 ORDER BY j.updated_at DESC LIMIT 5
verified_queries.explanation: Cancelled = status 12. JOIN for customer name (via created_by FK), contractor name, and job type name.

verified_queries.question: Which area has the most jobs?
verified_queries.sql: SELECT sa.title AS service_area, COUNT(j.id) AS job_count FROM jobs j JOIN properties p ON j.property_id = p.id JOIN service_areas sa ON p.service_area_id = sa.id WHERE j.status != 3 GROUP BY sa.title ORDER BY job_count DESC LIMIT 10
verified_queries.explanation: Jobs connect to service areas through properties: jobs.property_id → properties.service_area_id → service_areas.id. Never use job_service_areas for this — it maps job_types to areas for pricing.
